brief_title: Comparing Glycemic Outcomes of Carbohydrate Counting vs. Fixed Mealtime Insulin Dosing in Hospitalized Patients With Hyperglycemia
official_title: Comparing Glycemic Outcomes of Carbohydrate Counting vs. Fixed Mealtime Insulin Dosing in Hospitalized Patients With Hyperglycemia: an EHR-embedded Randomized Controlled Study
conditions: Hyperglycemia Due to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

interventions.name: Flexible fixed mealtime rapid-acting insulin dosing based on percentage of meal consumed

intervention_names: Other: Carbohydrate-counting-based prandial rapid-acting insulin dosing
arm_groups.label: Carbohydrate-Counting-Based Prandial Insulin Dosing

intervention_names: Other: Flexible fixed mealtime rapid-acting insulin dosing based on percentage of meal consumed
arm_groups.label: Flexible Fixed Mealtime Insulin Dosing

primary_outcomes.measure: Percentage of Time With Glucose in Target Range of 100 to 180 mg/dL
primary_outcomes.time_frame: From randomization to hospital discharge, up to 30 days

brief_summary: The study compares two current practices for calculating insulin dose for admitted patients: flexible fixed mealtime dosing based on percent of meal eaten and carbohydrate counting based on amount of carbohydrates eaten.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion criteria

* Adults ≥18 years
* Admitted to non-ICU units
* Require scheduled prandial insulin as part of basal-bolus insulin therapy with CC.

Exclusion criteria

* History of type 1 DM
* History of total pancreatectomy
* Use of pre-admission CC for prandial insulin administration
* Critical illness requiring ICU admission at time of recruitment.
* Admission to psychiatry services
* Pregnancy
* All forms of enteral/tube feeding or parenteral nutrition at recruitment
* Observation status at time of recruitment
